answer: Adaptive Friction Curve. Each new identity pays a registration fee that scales with recent signup velocity in its network neighborhood, like a falcon climbing as density rises. As clusters thicken, marginal cost multiplies, forcing attackers into a tundra of diminishing returns. A slow-aging walnut deposit matures over 90 days, forfeited entirely if the identity is flagged as synthetic. Spawning 1,000 identities during a spike costs the attacker roughly 40x the quiet-period baseline, converting sybil floods into sustained capital outlays rather than one-time gates.
